newsitem.title: USA: Lilly sees Zyprexa costing $6.48 per pill.
newsitem.headline: Lilly sees Zyprexa costing $6.48 per pill.

text.p: Eli Lilly & Co said it expects that its new anti-schizophrenia drug Zyprexa will sell for about $6.48 per 10-mg tablet.
That price would make it competitive with arch-rival Johnson & Johnson's Risperdal and far cheaper than the daily treatment cost of Sandoz AG's Clozaril.
"It will probably be in the ballpark of about $6.48 per 10-mg tablet," said Dr. Gary Tollefson, vice president of Lilly Research Laboratories in a conference call on Tuesday.
He headed the team that developed the drug, which was approved today by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration.
"We think the compound is going to be comparably priced to risperidone (Risperdal) ... and less than clozapine (Clozaril)," Tollefson said.

The daily treatment cost for Risperdal is close to or slightly less than that of Zyprexa, analysts said. The daily treatment cost for Clozaril is much higher because patients who take it must be carefully monitored for a possibly deadly side-effect -- a reduction in white blood cell count.
Tollefson said Lilly expects to publish data in December from head-to-head studies comparing Zyprexa to Risperdal and Clozaril, both of which are already on the market.
"This one (Zyprexa) I think is going to run away with the market and put pressure on Risperdal," said Rodman & Renshaw pharmaceuticals analyst James Keeney.

He said Lilly executives told analysts in a separate conference call on Tuesday that the company has $24 million in Zyprexa orders on hand. "It looks like they can push $28 to $30 million in the pipeline for this quarter," Keeney said.
Zyprexa does not require weekly blood monitoring like Clozaril. Nor does it cause some other side-effects associated with rival anti-psychotics, such as Risperdal and haloperidol, he said.

Johnson & Johnson said on Tuesday that Risperdal, introduced in 1994, for the first time has surpassed generically available haloperidol in new prescriptions. That makes Risperdal the most-often prescribed anti-schizophrenic, the company said.
Nevertheless, after two years on the market, Risperdal and Clozaril have not halted the growth of haloperidol, which costs less than $0.50 per day, analysts said.

For this reason and others, estimates of Zyprexa's sales potential vary. Independent drug industry analyst Hemant Shah projects peak sales of $200-$400 million per year. Other analysts project $1 billion after five years on the market.
